steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
A transformer processes a sequence (words, pixels, tokens, etc.) all at once rather than step-by-step.

1. Input embedding  
   Each token is turned into a vector; position information is added so the model knows order.

2. Self-attention  
   For every token, the model computes how much it should “pay attention” to every other token. These attention scores are used to mix information from the whole sequence, letting each token build a context-aware representation.

3. Multi-head attention  
   The attention step is done in parallel “heads,” so the model can learn different kinds of relationships (e.g., syntax, long-range dependencies) simultaneously.

4. Feed-forward layer  
   After attention, each token’s representation is passed through a small neural network to transform it further.

5. Stacking  
   Steps 2–4 are stacked in many identical layers, progressively refining representations.

6. Output  
   A final linear layer (and softmax for language tasks) turns the token representations into predictions (next word, class label, etc.).

Key idea: The transformer’s self-attention lets it relate every part of the input to every other part efficiently and in parallel, enabling powerful modeling of long-range dependencies.
